private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $350 rate was $76 above both competitors’ $274 rates, yet we received 190 hours and earned approximately $28,538. One quarter does not establish how much additional work a lower rate would attract.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest reduction to $325 rather than match competitors’ rates. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q1 before making further adjustments; avoid a price war without evidence it improves long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: Reducing the rate from $350 to $325 increased allocated hours from 190 to 295 and quarterly profit from approximately $28,538 to $36,930. Both competitors held at $274.
private_notes.plan: Test a further measured reduction to $300. The observed volume response suggests it may improve profit, while staying above competitors’ rates avoids an immediate match or undercut.

private_notes.observations: Reducing our rate from $350 to $300 increased allocated hours from 190 to 445 and quarterly profit from about $28,500 to $44,450. Both competitors have held at $274 throughout.
private_notes.plan: Test $275, just above the competitors’ stable rates. This should reveal whether approaching parity increases volume enough to offset the lower margin, without undercutting them.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood Hale and Calder Rowe have held their rates at $274 for four quarters. Reducing our rate from $350 to $275 steadily increased quarterly profit, reaching $48,039 in Q4. The allocation response below competitor parity remains untested.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest undercut at $265. Compare the additional hours and profit against Q4 to assess whether the volume gain offsets the lower margin.

private_notes.observations: With competitors steady at $274, profit peaked at our $275 rate ($48,039). Cutting to $265 increased hours from 641 to 731 but reduced profit to $47,484.
private_notes.plan: Return to $275, the best observed rate. Monitor competitor rates and allocations before making further adjustments.

private_notes.observations: Competitors have held rates at $274 throughout Q1–Q6. Our highest observed quarterly profit was $48,039 at a $275 rate, achieved in both Q4 and Q6; $265 and $300 yielded lower profits.
private_notes.plan: Keep the rate at $275. Review future allocations and rate cards for evidence that a different rate would improve long-run profit.
